<skills_instructions>
## Skills
A skill is a set of local instructions to follow that is stored in a `SKILL.md` file. Below is the list of skills that can be used. Each entry includes a name, description, and a short path that can be expanded into an absolute path using the skill roots table.
### Skill roots
- `r0` = `/tmp/codex-home/skills/.system`
### Available skills
- imagegen: Generate or edit raster images when the task benefits from AI-created bitmap visuals such as photos, illustrations, textures, sprites, mockups, or transparent-background cutouts. Use when Codex should create a brand-new image, transform an existing image, or derive visual variants from references, and the output should be a bitmap asset rather than repo-native code or vector. Do not use when the task is better handled by editing existing SVG/vector/code-native assets, extending an established icon or logo system, or building the visual directly in HTML/CSS/canvas. (file: r0/imagegen/SKILL.md)
- openai-docs: Use for Codex models/pricing, scheduled tasks, skills, settings, setup, troubleshooting, customization, automations, and self-knowledge—including 'you,' 'your,' 'this app,' or 'this coding agent' when they refer to Codex—and for OpenAI APIs/products and ChatGPT Work. Also use for model choice/migration, prompting, SDKs, Responses, Realtime, agents, evals, and Chat/Work/Codex comparisons. Do not use for generic app/software tasks that merely mention Codex. (file: r0/openai-docs/SKILL.md)
- skill-creator: Create or update a Codex skill with appropriately scoped instructions and any needed supporting resources. (file: r0/skill-creator/SKILL.md)
- skill-installer: Install Codex skills into $CODEX_HOME/skills from a curated list or a GitHub repo path. Use when a user asks to list installable skills, install a curated skill, or install a skill from another repo (including private repos). (file: r0/skill-installer/SKILL.md)
</skills_instructions><permissions instructions>
Filesystem sandboxing defines which files can be read or written. `sandbox_mode` is `danger-full-access`: No filesystem sandboxing - all commands are permitted. Network access is enabled.
Approval policy is currently never. Do not provide the `sandbox_permissions` for any reason, commands will be rejected.
</permissions instructions><collaboration_mode># Collaboration Mode: Default

You are now in Default mode. Any previous instructions for other modes (e.g. Plan mode) are no longer active.

Your active mode changes only when new developer instructions with a different `<collaboration_mode>...</collaboration_mode>` change it; user requests or tool descriptions do not change mode by themselves. Known mode names are Default and Plan.

## request_user_input availability

Use the `request_user_input` tool only when it is listed in the available tools for this turn.

Use the `request_user_input` tool only for optional questions where the answer would materially improve the quality of the work.

If `request_user_input` returns no answers, continue with best judgment instead of asking again or treating the turn as blocked.

Never use the `request_user_input` tool for permission requests or permission-related escalations.
</collaboration_mode>

<multi_agent_role>You are `/root`, the primary agent in a team of agents collaborating to fulfill the user's goals.

At the start of your turn, you are the active agent.
You can spawn sub-agents to handle subtasks, and those sub-agents can spawn their own sub-agents.
All agents in the team, including the agents that you can assign tasks to, are equally intelligent and capable, and have access to the same set of tools.

You can use `spawn_agent` to create a new agent, `followup_task` to give an existing agent a new task and trigger a turn, and `send_message` to pass a message to a running agent without triggering a turn.
`send_message` calls may be read by a human, so ensure they are legible. Always put proper spaces between words and/or numbers.
Child agents can also spawn their own sub-agents.
You can decide how much context you want to propagate to your sub-agents with the `fork_turns` parameter.

You will receive messages in the analysis channel in the form:
```
Message Type: MESSAGE | FINAL_ANSWER
Task name: <recipient>
Sender: <author>
Payload:
<payload text>
```
They may be addressed as to=/root

Note that collaboration tools cannot be called from inside `functions.exec`. Call `spawn_agent`, `send_message`, `followup_task`, `wait_agent`, `interrupt_agent`, and `list_agents` only as direct tool calls using the recipient shown in their tool definitions, such as `to=functions.collaboration.spawn_agent`, since they are intentionally absent from the `functions.exec` `tools.*` namespace. Available tools in `functions.exec` are explicitly described with a `tools` namespace in the developer message.

All agents share the same directory. In detail:
- All agents have access to the same container and filesystem as you.
- All agents use the same current working directory.
- As a result, edits made by one agent are immediately visible to all other agents.

When calling `wait_agent`, prefer longer waits (minutes) to avoid busy polling.

There are 4 available concurrency slots, meaning that up to 4 agents can be active at once, including you.

Full-history forks (`fork_turns` omitted or `"all"`) inherit the parent model and reasoning effort and do not accept overrides. Only set `model` or `reasoning_effort` when explicitly requested by the user, applicable `AGENTS.md` instructions, or skill instructions; when doing so, set `fork_turns` to `"none"`.</multi_agent_role>

<multi_agent_mode>Any earlier instruction enabling proactive multi-agent delegation no longer applies. Do not spawn sub-agents unless the user or applicable AGENTS.md/skill instructions explicitly ask for sub-agents, delegation, or parallel agent work.</multi_agent_mode>

# Improve the staged experiment

Review the staged post-training experiment and determine whether it is healthy
or unhealthy. Treat the workspace as a snapshot you may repair: inspect its
source, effective configuration, launch scripts, data processing, reward logic,
logs, tracked metrics, and frozen evaluation evidence. Do not assume that an
unusual setting or implementation is causal without connecting it to observed
behavior.

Use held-out evaluation evidence together with rollout, truncation, runtime,
optimization, and training signals. Training reward alone does not establish
held-out health.

## Your job

If you find a defect, fix it in the staged workspace at `/workspace`. **Do not
launch training.** Do not start the experiment, in the foreground or
background, and do not use `nohup`, `&`, `tmux`, `screen`, or any detach
mechanism. The system runs the experiment itself after you finish (see below);
mechanism. The system runs the experiment itself after you finish (see below);
anything you launch is wasted and scores nothing. Cheap, non-training checks
are fine.

When you are done, submit a report at `/workspace/report.md`. It must
summarize:

1. **Root cause** — the defect you found, and the evidence in the workspace
   (logs, metrics, code) that connects it to the observed behavior.
2. **Changes** — every file you changed and what you changed in it.
3. **Expected effect** — which metric the fix should move and in which
   direction.

A missing or empty `/workspace/report.md` scores 0.

## What the system will run

After you submit the report, the system deletes everything under
`$AUTORLBENCH_RESULTS/experiment_logs`, then re-runs the experiment in your
repaired workspace as a foreground process:

```bash
bash scripts/train.sh
```

with this environment:

```text
TRAINING_RUN_DIR=$AUTORLBENCH_RESULTS/experiment_logs
```

The effective run uses:

- model `/workspace/models/Qwen1.5-MoE-A2.7B-Chat`
- train data `/workspace/data/gsm8k/train.parquet` (7473 official training rows)
- validation data `/workspace/data/gsm8k/validation64.parquet` (the prepared 64 held-out rows)
- 150 training steps, validation at step 100 and the final step 150
- the supplied configuration, seeds, CP2/EP2/TP1 layout and two allocated GPUs
- `WANDB_MODE=offline`

The launcher places stdout under `experiment_logs/logs/train.log` and offline
W&B data under `experiment_logs/wandb`. The final held-out validation must be
logged at step 150; a step-0 score or an earlier best score is not sufficient.
A task-specific grading script then reads **only this fresh run's** files
under `$AUTORLBENCH_RESULTS/experiment_logs` and scores the key metrics; logs
written anywhere else are ignored. Keep the dataset, validation selection,
reward function, model, batch sizes, training budget and evaluation schedule
unchanged. Do not disable configured loss terms or parallelism to avoid an
implementation defect. Do not copy, edit, or fabricate metrics or replay
frozen historical logs as a new run. Otherwise the run is scored 0. Leave
frozen evidence under `observed_run/` intact.
I’ll inspect the code, effective configuration, and frozen training and evaluation evidence, then repair any defect the evidence supports. I won’t launch training.

steps.message: Held-out accuracy is 0/64 at both steps 100 and 150. I found a concrete mismatch: Megatron’s router z-loss expects token-count normalization, but this engine returns a loss format that supplies no token count. That leaves the auxiliary gradients unnormalized, consistent with the large gradients that persist after policy reward and policy loss reach zero.

from verl.workers.engine.megatron.transformer_impl import MegatronEngineWithLMHead
from megatron.core.pipeline_parallel.schedules import forward_step_calc_loss

from functools import partial

+"""Exercise MCore's loss callback and auxiliary autograd on CPU, without a model."""
+
+from functools import partial
+from types import SimpleNamespace
+from unittest.mock import patch
+
+import pytest
+import torch
+from megatron.core.pipeline_parallel.schedules import forward_step_calc_loss
+from megatron.core.transformer.moe.moe_utils import MoEAuxLossAutoScaler, z_loss_func
+from megatron.core.transformer.moe.router import TopKRouter

+from verl.utils import tensordict_utils as tu

+
+
+def _engine(*, cp_size=1, per_token=True):
+    engine = object.__new__(MegatronEngineWithLMHead)
+    engine.engine_config = SimpleNamespace(dynamic_context_parallel=False, use_remove_padding=True)
+    engine.tf_config = SimpleNamespace(
+        calculate_per_token_loss=per_token,
+        num_moe_experts=60,
+        moe_z_loss_coeff=0.001,
+        moe_aux_loss_coeff=0.0,
+        mtp_num_layers=None,
+        num_layers=24,
+        fp8=None,
+        timers=None,
+        grad_scale_func=None,
+    )
+    engine.get_data_parallel_group = lambda: None
+    router = SimpleNamespace(
+        config=engine.tf_config,
+        tp_cp_group=SimpleNamespace(size=lambda: cp_size),
+        calculate_per_token_loss=per_token,
+        training=True,
+        layer_number=None,
+    )
+    return engine, router
+
+
+def _batch(lengths, *, num_micro_batch=1, dp_size=1, total_input_tokens=None):
+    input_ids = torch.nested.nested_tensor([torch.arange(n) for n in lengths], layout=torch.jagged)
+    return tu.assign_non_tensor(
+        TensorDict({"input_ids": input_ids}, batch_size=[len(lengths)]),
+        num_micro_batch=num_micro_batch,
+        dp_size=dp_size,
+        batch_num_input_tokens=total_input_tokens or sum(lengths),
+        batch_num_tokens=sum(lengths),
+    )
+
+
+@pytest.fixture(autouse=True)
+def _restore_aux_scale():
+    previous = MoEAuxLossAutoScaler.main_loss_backward_scale
+    MoEAuxLossAutoScaler.main_loss_backward_scale = None
+    yield
+    MoEAuxLossAutoScaler.main_loss_backward_scale = previous
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("total_tokens", [4, 64, 1024])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("num_microbatches", [1, 2, 4])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("cp_size", [1, 2])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("dp_size", [1, 2])
+def test_policy_and_z_loss_match_global_objective(total_tokens, num_microbatches, cp_size, dp_size):
+    """Real router z-loss and MCore scheduling must preserve the global objective.
+
+    Each CPU loop iteration represents a DP/CP rank; summing its scalar gradient
+    represents DDP's SUM collective. No model or optimizer is constructed.
+    """
+    engine, router = _engine(cp_size=cp_size)
+    total_input_tokens = total_tokens * dp_size
+    micro_lengths = [total_tokens // num_microbatches] * num_microbatches
+    actual_gradient = 0.0
+    for dp_rank in range(dp_size):
+        for cp_rank in range(cp_size):
+            theta = torch.tensor(0.25, requires_grad=True)
+            local_count = 0
+            for micro_length in micro_lengths:
+                count = len(range(cp_rank, micro_length, cp_size))
+                logits = theta.expand(count, 4)
+                attached = TopKRouter.apply_z_loss(router, logits)
+
+                def loss_function(model_output, **kwargs):
+                    # Mirrors globally normalized PPO/KL output after CP gather:
+                    # only this rank's tokens retain their autograd graph.
+                    return model_output["log_probs"].sum() * dp_size / total_input_tokens, {}
+
+                data = _batch(
+                    [micro_length],
+                    num_micro_batch=num_microbatches,
+                    dp_size=dp_size,
+                    total_input_tokens=total_input_tokens,
+                )
+                callback = partial(
+                    engine.postprocess_micro_batch_func,
+                    data=data,
+                    forward_only=False,
+                    loss_function=loss_function,
+                    num_tokens=torch.tensor(count),
+                )
+                loss, num_tokens = forward_step_calc_loss(
+                    None,
+                    {"log_probs": attached},
+                    callback,
+                    engine.tf_config,
+                    None,
+                    False,
+                    num_microbatches,
+                    [],
+                    cp_group_size=cp_size,
+                    is_last_stage=True,
+                )
+                loss.backward()
+                local_count += num_tokens.item()
+            assert local_count == len(range(cp_rank, total_tokens, cp_size))
+            # finalize_model_grads sums the local counts and divides the reduced gradient.
+            actual_gradient += theta.grad / total_input_tokens
+
+    truth = torch.tensor(0.25, requires_grad=True)
+    expected_loss = truth * 4 + z_loss_func(truth.expand(total_input_tokens, 4), 0.001 / cp_size)
+    expected_gradient = torch.autograd.grad(expected_loss, truth)[0]
+    torch.testing.assert_close(actual_gradient, expected_gradient)
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("lengths", [[5, 7, 10], [1, 2, 3], [13]])
+def test_cp_padding_is_excluded_from_router_loss_and_final_token_count(lengths):
+    engine, router = _engine(cp_size=2)
+    counted_tokens = 0
+    for cp_rank in range(2):
+        with (
+            patch("verl.models.mcore.util.mpu.get_tensor_model_parallel_world_size", return_value=1),
+            patch("verl.models.mcore.util.mpu.get_context_parallel_world_size", return_value=2),
+            patch("verl.models.mcore.util.mpu.get_context_parallel_rank", return_value=cp_rank),
+        ):
+            kwargs, count = engine._prepare_per_token_loss_inputs(_batch(lengths))
+        padding_mask = kwargs["router_padding_mask"]
+        counted_tokens += count.item()
+        expected_rows = sum((n + 3) // 4 * 4 for n in lengths) // 2
+        assert padding_mask.shape == (1, expected_rows)
+        assert count.item() == (~padding_mask).sum().item()
+        theta = torch.tensor(0.25, requires_grad=True)
+        logits = theta.expand(expected_rows, 4)
+        logits.retain_grad()
+        attached = TopKRouter.apply_z_loss(router, logits, padding_mask=padding_mask.flatten())
+        attached.sum().mul(0).backward()
+        assert torch.count_nonzero(logits.grad[padding_mask.flatten()]) == 0
+    assert counted_tokens == sum(lengths)
+
+
+def test_forward_only_keeps_two_value_callback_and_unscaled_metrics():
+    engine, _ = _engine(cp_size=2)
+    data = _batch([8])
+    result = engine.postprocess_micro_batch_func({}, data, forward_only=True, loss_function=None)
+    assert len(result) == 2
+    assert result[1]["loss"] == 1.0
+    with torch.no_grad():
+        assert engine._prepare_per_token_loss_inputs(data) == ({}, None)
+
+
+def test_legacy_non_per_token_callback_is_unchanged():
+    engine, _ = _engine(per_token=False)
+    data = _batch([8], num_micro_batch=4)
+    loss = torch.tensor(0.25, requires_grad=True)
+    scaled, stats = engine.postprocess_micro_batch_func(
+        {}, data, forward_only=False, loss_function=lambda **kwargs: (loss, {"metric": 3.0})
+    )
+    torch.testing.assert_close(scaled, loss * 4)
+    assert stats["loss"] == 0.25
+    assert stats["metrics"] == {"metric": 3.0}
+
+
+def test_per_token_callback_preserves_reported_loss_and_metrics():
+    engine, _ = _engine(cp_size=2)
+    data = _batch([8], num_micro_batch=4)
+    loss = torch.tensor(0.25, requires_grad=True)
+    scaled, count, stats = engine.postprocess_micro_batch_func(
+        {},
+        data,
+        forward_only=False,
+        loss_function=lambda **kwargs: (loss, {"metric": 3.0}),
+        num_tokens=torch.tensor(4),
+    )
+    torch.testing.assert_close(scaled, loss * 8)
+    assert count.item() == 4
+    assert stats["loss"] == 0.25
+    assert stats["metrics"] == {"metric": 3.0}

text(await tools.apply_patch("*** Begin Patch
*** Add File: /workspace/report.md
+# Staged Experiment Review
+
+## Root Cause
+
+**Verdict: unhealthy.** The frozen run completed 150 steps, but held-out
+`val-core/openai/gsm8k/acc/mean@1` is **0.0 (0/64)** at both step 100 and
+step 150. These are actual post-update evaluations, recorded in
+`observed_run/console-history.jsonl` and `observed_run/stdout.log:2454,3033`.
+The final validation summary is at `observed_run/stdout.log:3035`.
+Offline W&B independently records the step-100 failure. Its history ends at
+148, as documented in `observed_run/logging-limitation.txt`; the console
+provides the final two steps. There is no measured pre-training validation
+baseline, so an exact held-out accuracy decline cannot be claimed.
+
+The defect is the **Megatron per-token loss integration**, specifically
+`src/framework/verl/workers/engine/megatron/transformer_impl.py`:
+
+- The effective configuration enables `calculate_per_token_loss: true`,
+  `moe_z_loss_coeff: 0.001`, PPO/KL loss, CP2, EP2 and TP1. This is confirmed
+  by `observed_run/resolved-config.yaml` and the actual TransformerConfig
+  printed at `observed_run/stdout.log:1030`. Load-balancing loss is disabled,
+  but router z-loss is still enabled.
+- Megatron-Core 0.16's `TopKRouter.apply_z_loss` multiplies z-loss by the
+  local router token count in per-token mode. `MoEAuxLossAutoScaler`
+  injects its gradient independently of the scalar PPO loss. The schedule
+  expects token counts from a three-value loss callback, then
+  `finalize_model_grads` divides accumulated gradients by the global count.
+- The staged engine instead returned the legacy two-value callback. MCore
+  therefore accumulated a zero token count and skipped gradient division.
+  The auxiliary-loss guard also bypassed its existing DP/CP compensation
+  when z-loss was enabled. Scalar `actor/loss` reports PPO/KL only, hiding
+  the unnormalized router gradient.
+- A CPU reproduction using the installed MCore schedule and auxiliary
+  autograd confirmed that the old callback reported **zero tokens** and
+  inflated z-loss gradients by **4x, 64x and 1024x** for batches with those
+  token counts. This establishes an implementation error, rather than
+  attributing collapse to an unusual coefficient alone.
+
+The observed progression is consistent with that unintended optimization:
+
+| Frozen Training Window | Mean Reward | Mean Response Tokens | Truncation Ratio | Mean Gradient Norm | Mean Generation Seconds |
+| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
+| Steps 1-10 | 0.15625 | 213.76 | 0.00625 | 301.66 | 17.42 |
+| Steps 26-50 | 0.35500 | 243.09 | 0.00500 | 170.36 | 18.92 |
+| Steps 101-125 | 0.00000 | 961.32 | 0.86250 | 120.89 | 50.74 |
+| Steps 126-150 | 0.00000 | 1010.02 | 0.96500 | 129.28 | 50.75 |
+
+At step 150, reward, advantages, policy loss and PPO clipping fraction are
+all zero, every response reaches 1024 tokens, yet gradient norm is 188.35
+with a reported PPO/KL loss of only 0.0002161. The gradients are therefore
+not evidence of productive policy learning. Late rollout/actor probability
+correlation remains about 0.997; weight updates continue to complete.
+Prompt clipping and aborted-response ratios remain zero. No nonfinite
+numeric metrics were found. Generation becomes slower as responses saturate
+the cap, while weight-transfer time stays near 65 seconds. This supports
+loss-driven degeneration, rather than prompt truncation, failed transfers
+or a runtime crash. Training reward's temporary rise does not establish
+held-out health.
+
+Data/reward review found no defect: prepared parquet hashes match
+`metadata/gsm8k-provenance.json`; all 7473 official training rows and the
+exact seeded 64 held-out examples are retained; train/test questions are
+disjoint. Every stored ground-truth answer passes the existing strict
+`#### answer` reward, and wrong/missing answers receive zero.
+
+## Changes
+
+1. `src/framework/verl/workers/engine/megatron/transformer_impl.py`
+   - Use MCore's three-value loss callback for the staged static-CP packed
+     per-token path, returning the local valid input-token count.
+   - Compute the global valid prompt-plus-response count independently of
+     the response-only denominator used by PPO/KL.
+   - Multiply the already-normalized policy loss by global input tokens
+     divided by DP size, compensating for MCore's final token division
+     without the legacy microbatch/CP multiplication.
+   - Construct router padding masks with the existing THD packing helper,
+     so CP alignment padding contributes neither z-loss nor token count.
+   - Carry counts through both language and value head forward callbacks.
+     Keep evaluation and specialized MTP/attention/dynamic-CP paths on
+     their existing behavior. Reported loss and metrics retain their
+     original, unscaled values.
+2. `src/framework/tests/workers/test_megatron_per_token_normalization_on_cpu.py`
+   - Add CPU regression coverage using the real MCore loss schedule,
+     router z-loss and auxiliary autograd. Cover CP1/CP2, DP1/DP2,
+     token counts, microbatch splits, padding, callback plumbing, separate
+     input/response denominators, evaluation and legacy behavior.
+3. `report.md`
+   - Add this diagnosis, evidence, change inventory and expected effects.
+
+No experiment configuration, dataset, selection, reward, model, batch size,
+seed, training budget, evaluation schedule, parallelism or runtime hook was
+changed. All frozen `observed_run/` evidence remains intact.
+
+## Verification and Expected Effect
+
+Non-training verification: **50 passed, 1 skipped** across the new regression
+suite, existing Megatron distillation tests and preprocessing tests. The
+skipped test requires CUDA. Also passed Python syntax checks, `bash -n
+scripts/train.sh`, read-only Hydra composition with the launcher's exact
+overrides, dataset hashes/selection and reward checks.
+
+The launcher still uses `TRAINING_RUN_DIR` for stdout, offline W&B,
+validation generations and checkpoints. Its overrides retain validation
+at 100; the trainer explicitly validates after the final update at 150
+and logs those metrics at 150. The existing runtime hook explicitly
+finishes W&B after that final log, addressing the frozen history's teardown
+limitation without synthesizing records.
+
+Expected directions for the fresh run:
+
+- **Increase final step-150 held-out `val-core/openai/gsm8k/acc/mean@1`**
+  above the frozen 0/64 result by preserving meaningful PPO/KL learning.
+- **Decrease late `response_length/clip_ratio` and response length**, from
+  near-total cap saturation toward terminating solutions.
+- **Decrease `actor/grad_norm`** and persistent clipping pressure caused
+  by auxiliary gradients that previously scaled with total tokens.
+- **Increase late `critic/score/mean`** and restore informative GRPO
+  advantages; **decrease generation time** as truncation subsides.
+
+These are expected effects, not measured results of repaired training.
+**Training was not launched.** No frozen metrics were copied, modified or
+replayed as a fresh run, and no new experiment results were fabricated.
*** End Patch"));
